datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: Universal Dependencies POS uses independently annotated treebanks in each language. WikiANN uses automatically annotated Wikipedia in each language. TyDiQA-GoldP uses questions written by native speakers in each language. BUCC uses parallel corpora from comparable sources. Tatoeba uses community-contributed sentence pairs.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: XNLI: 'Crowd-sourced English data is translated to ten other languages by professional translators.' PAWS-X: 'A subset of the PAWS dev and test sets was translated to six other languages by professional translators.' XQuAD: 'A subset of the English SQuAD v1.1 dev set was translated into ten other languages by professional translators.'

details.Universal Dependencies POS: Treebanks created from native text in each language with independently annotated data
details.TyDiQA-GoldP: Questions written by native speakers reflecting natural information-seeking behavior in each language, without seeing the answers

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: Only TyDiQA-GoldP clearly uses native speaker annotators for question creation. XNLI, PAWS-X, and XQuAD use professional translators (not necessarily native speakers of target languages). WikiANN uses fully automatic annotation. MLQA uses English crowdsource workers. Paper does not provide details on annotator native-speaker status for BUCC, Tatoeba, or Universal Dependencies POS.

creator_types_across_datasets: crowdworkers (XNLI original English, MLQA English questions)
annotator_workforce.evidence: Paper does not report annotator demographics, compensation, or ethics review. The XTREME paper aggregates existing datasets and does not create new annotations. Annotator details are in the original dataset papers.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: XTREME is explicitly English-centric in its evaluation design: 'XTREME focuses on the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer scenario, where annotated training data is provided in English but none is provided in the language to which systems must transfer.' Three of nine datasets (XNLI, PAWS-X, XQuAD) are direct translations from English. MLQA questions originate in English. All models are trained on English data and evaluated on other languages. The paper acknowledges: 'English is not generally the best source language for cross-lingual transfer for all target languages.'

notably_excluded: Most of Sub-Saharan Africa (only Swahili and Yoruba)
geographic_representation.evidence: XTREME covers 40 languages from 12 language families and two isolates: Afro-Asiatic, Austro-Asiatic, Austronesian, Dravidian, Indo-European, Japonic, Kartvelian, Kra-Dai, Niger-Congo, Sino-Tibetan, Turkic, and Uralic. However, the benchmark acknowledges limitations: 'while models do reasonably well in most languages in the Indo-European family, we observe lower performance particularly for Sino-Tibetan, Japonic, Koreanic, and Niger-Congo languages.' Indo-European languages are heavily overrepresented with ~17 of 40 languages.
